title: introduce-harmony-stitch-attn-kernel-and-continuous-prefetch-microbatcher
author: Arjun Patel
description: Context: Production traffic showed tail-latency variability for mid-length chat requests when running the existing flash-style attn paths under mixed sequence lengths. Motivation: Reduce scheduled prefetch stalls, shrink KV-cache warmup time, and get better single-GPU throughput without regressing long-sequence stability. This PR introduces the "Harmony Stitch" attention kernel (a stitched microkernel that interleaves rotary offset compaction with a lightweight fused qkv transpose) and a continuous prefetch microbatcher that coordinates KV preheat lanes across inflight requests. Highlights: 1) New kernel: harmony_stitch_attn.cpp/h — stitches small tiled GEMM passes to reduce global memory pressure and expose a fast path for rotary/rope-aware offsets. The implementation uses: - compact rotary index packing to avoid per-token modulus ops, - interleaved qkv transform to amortize memory write traffic, - a short hotpath (<=32 tokens) that avoids large kernel launches for streaming tokens. 2) Prefetch microbatcher: continuous_prefetcher.cc — a low-overhead scheduler that groups inflight requests by rotary-offset locality and sequence-length bucket, issuing staged KV preheat requests to the serving runtime while respecting latency SLO hints. It leverages affinity hints from the request router to keep KV stripes warm on the same GPU when possible. 3) KV-cache warmup improvements: warmup heuristics now include a 'lane-priority' score which biases eviction decisions to preserve recently used rotary offset ranges; this reduces repeated warmup thrash for chat-style turn-taking patterns. 4) Quantization/precision: harmony path retains fp16 accumulators but uses fp32 reductions for rotary index arithmetic to avoid tiny bias drifts observed in earlier fp16-only paths. 5) Testing and metrics: new microbenchmarks (bench/harmony_stitch_bench) and end-to-end load tests showing median latency down 7-12% and peak throughput up ~18% on A100-40GB for our conversational workload with mixed seq len [8..512]. Changes in this PR: - New kernel source and header files under src/runtime/attn/ - Continuous prefetch scheduler and tests under src/runtime/scheduler/ - Runtime hooks to expose per-request rotary locality hints - Unit tests and integration tests covering correctness vs existing flashbridge kernel - Bench harness and CI job (ci/perf/harmony) Backwards compatibility: Default behavior is unchanged. The harmony path is opt-in via the "ATTN_HARMONY" runtime flag and enabled by policy for dedicated pools after runtime compatibility checks. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pools -> broader Dedicated rollout -> optional opt-in for Hosted customers via model policy. Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests - [x] Scheduler and integration tests - [x] Microbenchmarks added and run on internal perf lab - [x] CI perf gate added (smoke) - [x] Documentation notes for ops team Commits: see commit list below. Risks and mitigations: - Edge-case rotary alignment bugs: added property-based test harness that fuzzes rotary offsets across batch boundaries. - Memory pinning behavior: added fallback path that reverts to existing flashbridge kernel if warmup allocator fails. - Regression in fp16 accumulation: kept fp32 reduction path and regression checks in CI. Merge: squash and merge after approvals. Related: This complements ENG-2158 (prefetch policy review) and was motivated by a customer incident SUP-1198 (KV warmup causing 5xx spikes).

review_comments: Sofia Martinez: Overall this looks promising. Please add a short doc explaining the failure mode that triggers fallback to flashbridge (so SREs can triage).
Author (Arjun): Good point — added docs/ops/harmony-attn.md with a section on fallback signals and diagnostics.

release_notes: Introduce Harmony Stitch attention kernel (opt-in). Improves median latency by 7-12% and throughput by ~18% for mixed conversational workloads; KV warmup improved to reduce warmup churn in chat patterns. Opt-in via ATTN_HARMONY flag; see ops docs for rollout guidance.
